checks: No eclipse at 105 of 201 covered epochs where the 1.05226 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 86934109 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.0523 days. Data from the TESS mission show a primary eclipse with a depth of 0.46% dimming, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 111.8 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 17.0, though the centroid offset of 3.7 arcseconds from the target location warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown. All data quality checks passed without flag warnings, supporting the reliability of this automated detection from photometric and image analysis.
